page.layout: One page of text; running head at top centre; epigram lines in italic verse above a rule, then a centred title in roman, then a stanza with large initial V; catchword "Foedif-" at lower right. No margin notes.

p.i: Quod luit ille sua, mox, latro morte scelestus.
Et Reges cura quis neget esse Deo?
Quem si, Henrice, coles, quem nactus vereare? scelesti

main_text.head: In illum Parricidam grauissimo quidem sed iustissimo supplicio affectum.
main_text.p:
VVlneribus Vulnus puniri pluribus Unum,
Sauitia non est cur videatur opus:

p.i: Vulnere nam quanuis Unus peteretur in Uno,
Gallia Rege tamen quum salua sit omnis in Uno,
Omnis in hoc casu sic peritura fuit.
Adde quod Unius non haec sunt artibus acta,
Sed sceleris consors est scelerata cohors,
Iesum, inquam, mentita cohors, qua fretus Iberus
Ah potius scelleri poena ut respondeat ultrix,
Ipse tuum & nostrum, Christe, tuere decus.
Sic, o Rex, Verum Vere Venerator Iesum,
Sic Regem agnoscat Gallia salua suum.

page.notes: The first stanza is set in italic with a large decorated initial V; the scan is damaged at the right edge and the lower part of the left, and several letters in the verse are doubtful, notably in the lines beginning "Vulnere" and "Adde quod". The lines marked "Sic" in the last couplet are partly obscured. The word "Fœdif-" at the foot is a catchword.
